The '''Folgar-Tucker-Equation (FTE)''' is a widespread and commercially applied model to describe the fiber orientation in injection molding simulations of fiber composites.

The equation is based on [[Jeffery–Hamel flow|Jeffrey's equation]] for fibers suspended in melts, but, in addition, accounts for fiber-fiber interactions.<ref>{{Cite journal
 | author = F. Folgar and C. L. Tucker
 | year = 1984
 | title = Orientation Behavior of Fibers in Concentrated Suspensions
 | journal = Journal of Reinforced Plastics and Composites
 | volume =3 
 | issue = 2
 | pages = 98–119
 | doi = 10.1177/073168448400300201
 | bibcode =1984JRPC....3...98F
 | s2cid =137183305
 | id = 
 | url = 
 }}</ref>
Tucker and Advani then integrate over an ensemble of fibers and hence obtain an evolution equation for the orientation/alignment tensor<ref>{{Cite journal
 | author = S. G. Advani and C. L. Tucker
 | year = 1987
 | title = The use of tensors to describe and predict fiber orientation in short fiber composites
 | journal = Journal of Rheology
 | volume =31 
 | issue = 8
 | pages = 751–784 
 | doi =10.1122/1.549945
 | bibcode =1987JRheo..31..751A
 | id = 
 | url = 
 }}</ref>
as a [[Field (physics)]].
A compact way to express it is<ref>{{Cite journal
 | author = C. L. Tucker and J.G. O'Gara and J. Wang
 | year = 2008
 | title = An objective model for slow orientation kinetics in concentrated fiber suspensions: Theory and rheological evidence
 | journal = Journal of Rheology
 | volume =52 
 | issue = 5
 | pages = 751–784 
 | doi =10.1122/1.2946437
 | bibcode =2008JRheo..52.1179W
 | id = 
 | url = 
 }}</ref>

<math>
    \frac{dA}{dt}=W\cdot A-A\cdot W+\xi(D\cdot A+ A\cdot D-2A_4:D)+2C\dot{\gamma}(1-3A).
</math>

The scalar quantities are the shear rate <math>\dot{\gamma}</math>, the interaction coefficient C (for an isotropic diffusion) and the parameter accounting for the fibers aspect ratio <math>\xi</math>. <math>A_4</math> is a fourth order tensor. Normally, <math>A_4</math> is expressed as a function of A. The detection of the best suited function is known as closure problem.
D and W are respectively the symmetric and antisymmetric part of the velocity gradient, while 1 represents the unit tensor.
<math>:</math> represents a contraction over two indices.

Thus the Folgar Tucker is a differential equation for the second order [[tensor]] A, namely the orientation tensor.
This evolution equation is in the frame of [[continuum mechanics]] and is coupled to the velocity field.

Since different closure forms can be inserted, many possible formulations of the equations are possible.<ref>{{Cite book
 | author = Peter K. Kennedy
 | author2= Rong Zheng
 | year = 2013
 | title = Flow Analysis of Injections Molds
 | publisher = Hanser
 | location = 
 | isbn = 
 | pages = 80–84
}}</ref> For most of the closure forms the FTE results in a nonlinear [[differential equation]] (though a Lemma to linearize it for some popular closure was introduced <ref name=":0">{{Cite journal
 | author = A. Winters and C. Papenfuss and M. Karow
 | year = 2022
 | title = Benchmarking solutions of the Folgar–Tucker-Equation and its reduction to a linear problem for non-linear closure forms
 | journal = Journal of Non-Newtonian Fluid Mechanics
 | volume = 310 
 | issue = 
 | article-number =104922
 | doi = 10.1016/j.jnnfm.2022.104922
 | bibcode = 2022JNNFM.31004922W
 | s2cid =252928015
 | id = 
 | url = https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0377025722001410
 | hdl = 20.500.11850/577274
 | hdl-access = free
 }}</ref>).

Analytical solutions to some versions of the FTE consists of both exponential, trigonometrical and hyperbolic functions.<ref name=":0" />

Numerically the FTE is solved also in commercial software for injection molding simulations.
